raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Allow MoE implementations to provide an optional shared routing-row restorer, so backends such as vLLM-Ascend can restore their token layout without replacing `capture()`. The existing upstream recovery algorithm remains the default.

Related to #61539. This consolidates the smaller implementation from #65321 into this PR.

## Claims

- Bind the first available `restore_routed_experts_rows(topk_ids, ctx)` method once for all captured layers. Existing capture sources need no changes.
- Preserve `_restore_local_topk_ids(topk_ids, ctx)`, capture/router signatures, microbatch offsets and buffer writes.
- Limit production changes to `routed_experts_capturer.py`; no changes to MoERunner, MegaMoE, ModelRunner or ForwardContext.

## Validation

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu VLLM_PLUGINS='' HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -o addopts='' \
  tests/model_executor/test_routed_experts_capture.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_ubatch_slicing.py -q
```

The previous head (`a109c1d`) produced **79 passed, 10 skipped** on CPU. The current head (`329840b`) replaces the broad parametrized test with two focused cases: exact buffer writes from one custom restorer, and use of the current forward context across two distinct layers. These cases have not yet been rerun on the current head.

Applicable pre-commit checks (including mypy and CI test selection) and `git diff --check` passed on the previous head; current-head local validation is pending. GPU-dependent skips are not graph-replay validation.

## Details

The selected restorer must handle every captured MoE layer using the current forward context, without depending on its provider's layer-specific state. It owns any required communication and padding removal. Providers must keep collectives rank-consistent and graph-replay safe.

This retains upstream shape inference and existing buffer semantics; it does not add per-layer restoration strategies or combine records written to the same layer slot.

### vLLM-Ascend integration

A local adapter was checked against the pre-rebase #65321 revision with 35 isolated CPU tests and 20 subtests. These exercise callback binding and restored buffer contents, including padded MC2/SP rows, with mocked collectives. NPU/HCCL, full-model serving and graph replay have not been validated for this implementation.

---

- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Relevant checks passed and the optional hook contract is documented.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Scope, motivation, related PR and validation boundaries are described.

🚀

Validation review of `a109c1d29ac1e4873836e800e9839a3d8ebdab5a` (with #65321 consolidated).

**Environment:** 4× H20 (GPU 0–3), `vllm_liam` container. I reviewed the changed binding/capture code: the optional shared restorer is selected once, and the original `_restore_local_topk_ids` remains the default when no provider is present. I found no blocking issue in this diff.

**Capture accuracy:** For each forward, an independent oracle recomputed routing IDs from the router inputs before expert dispatch; it did not invoke the capturer or restorer. I compared the raw capture buffer's valid entries element by element with the oracle, then checked the returned routed-expert IDs at each client token position. Across 46 requests, **1,368,496 client ID elements and 5,693,952 valid buffer ID elements had zero mismatches**:

| Model / mode | Parallelism and execution | Requests | Buffer mismatches | Shared-restorer calls |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-30B-A3B FP8, FULL default | DP2/TP2, EP/SP, DeepEP low-latency, DBO | 14 | 0 / 1,605,888 | 0 |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B FP8, FULL hook | Same | 14 | 0 / 1,605,888 | 10,368 |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B FP8, PIECEWISE hook | TP2, EP | 5 | 0 / 568,320 | 2,016 |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B FP8, eager hook | DP2/TP2, EP/SP | 8 | 0 / 1,165,056 | 20,160 |
| Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B, generic MoERunner + FULL hook | TP4, EP (no SP/DBO) | 5 | 0 / 748,800 | 2,600 |

The test-side shared restorer delegates the existing recovery algorithm, so these GPU runs validate binding and capture integration, not a distinct backend restoration algorithm

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

DeepSeek V4.1 capture-accuracy follow-up on 8×H20 (TP8, DP1, FULL CUDA Graph, generic MoERunner/MXFP4 Marlin; no EP/SP/DBO). I added three stress workloads to the earlier mixed-length case:

| Input / output tokens | Concurrency | Requests | Client IDs checked | 8-GPU buffer IDs checked | Mismatches |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 128 or 512 / 64 (existing) | 16 | 32 | 2,941,440 | 29,754,240 | 0 |
| 512 or 1024 / 128 (new) | 16 | 32 | 6,873,600 | 54,988,800 | 0 |
| 128 or 256 / 256 (new) | 16 | 32 | 3,432,960 | 27,463,680 | 0 |
| 128 or 256 / 64 (new) | 32 | 64 | 3,916,800 | 31,334,400 | 0 |

Each workload ran two rounds. I independently recomputed the per-layer router top-k IDs before dispatch, compared them exactly with the captured device buffer after each step, and compared reconstructed per-request token positions with returned `routed_experts`. In total: 160 distinct requests, 17,164,800 returned IDs and 143,541,120 buffer IDs checked, **0 mismatches**. All 40 routed layers and top-6 IDs were covered. The concurrency-32 run explicitly captured graph size 32 and recorded 127 graph replays per GPU.

Tested commit: `a59d604c945ed149bfbf597468ff05fbea73ec3a`. Current head `2a6aefb1456cc743e3f6d7a992dae2e3cbc31962` differs only in test files; the production capture implementation is unchanged. I have not rerun the GPU workload on that exact head. This reports accuracy only, not performance.

Updated DeepSeek V4.1 validation review — supersedes my earlier DeepSeek-only review at https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64689#pullrequestreview-5766778010.

Validation follow-up: DeepSeek V4.1 capture accuracy on PR commit `a59d604c945ed149bfbf597468ff05fbea73ec3a`.

**Environment:** 8× H20 (GPU 0–7), `vllm_liam`. The three TP8 rows use the complete DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash weights and generic MoERunner/MXFP4 Marlin. The DP4/TP2 row uses a **reduced V4.1 configuration with dummy weights** (4 routed layers, 8 experts) because the complete 475 GiB checkpoint cannot fit at TP2 on 96 GiB H20s. That row exercises the V4.1 routing/capture and DP/EP/SP integration, not full-model weight loading.

**Capture accuracy:** An independent oracle recomputed each layer's router top-k IDs before expert dispatch without calling the capturer or restorer. I compared valid device-buffer entries element by element with that oracle and checked returned `routed_experts` at each client token position. Each row ran two rounds.

| Model / mode | Parallelism and execution | Input / output tokens; concurrency | Requests | Buffer mismatches | Shared-restorer calls |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| V4.1 full weights, long-input stress | DP1/TP8, FULL Graph, no EP/SP | 512 or 1024 / 128; C16 | 32 | 0 / 54,988,800 | 4,800 |
| V4.1 full weights, high-concurrency stress | DP1/TP8, FULL Graph (capture size 32), no EP/SP | 128 or 256 / 64; C32 | 64 | 0 / 31,334,400 | 2,880 |
| V4.1 **reduced config, dummy weights** | DP4/TP2, EP/SP, FULL Graph | 128 or 256 / 64; C8 per DP rank | 64 total | 0 / 1,395,936 | 864 |
| V4.1 full weights | DP1/TP8, EP (no SP), PIECEWISE Graph | 128 or 256 / 64; C8 | 16 | 0 / 13,933,440 | 8,960 |

Returned route IDs also had **0 mismatches** in every row. The two full-weight stress rows checked 6,873,600 and 3,916,800 returned IDs, respectively; the DP4/TP2 dummy row checked 391,680; the full-weight PIECEWISE row checked 979,200. Execution counters confirmed graph-path use: 254 and 127 FULL graph replays per GPU for the stress rows, 154 FULL replays per GPU for DP4/TP2, and 127 PIECEWISE graph calls per GPU for the final row.

V4.1 Engram rejects DBO/microbatching at configuration validation, so **DBO was not enabled** in these V4.1 cases. The test-side shared restorer delegates the existing recovery algorithm; these tests validate binding and capture integration, not a separate backend restoration algorithm. No performance claim is made here.

The current PR head is `2a6aefb1456cc743e3f6d7a992dae2e3cbc31962`; relative to the tested commit, only test files changed, not the production capture implementation. The exact current head was not GPU-rerun.

 Routing is stored by the aux output connector (`vllm/distributed/aux_output_connector/`, configured via `--aux-output-config`), keyed by KV block hash and shared with prefix caching, which is why prefix caching is required. `max_bytes` is its host-memory LRU capacity (default: derived from KV cache capacity). If a prefix-cache hit needs evicted rows, the worker raises `BlockObjectStoreError`; increase `max_bytes`.
 
+### Backend row restoration
+
+A backend's `MoERunner` or `RoutedExpertsCaptureSource` can optionally implement
+`restore_routed_experts_rows(topk_ids, ctx) -> Tensor`. During binding, the capturer
+selects the first such module in `model.modules()` order and uses its callback
+for every captured layer. Without a provider, the existing DP/TP recovery is used.
+Existing capture sources need no changes.
+
+The callback must restore this DP rank's token-ordered logical expert IDs for all
+captured layers, using the supplied `ForwardContext` rather than the provider's
+layer-specific state. It must preserve the input, device, dtype and top-k width,
+and keep collective participation consistent across ranks, including empty
+ranks. Operations must support graph replay. Models requiring different per-layer
+restorers cannot use this hook. Repeated layer IDs do not select a different
+restorer; the existing buffer-write semantics are unchanged.
+

Updated DeepSeek V4.1 validation review — supersedes my earlier DeepSeek-only review at https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64689#pullrequestreview-5766778010.

Validation follow-up: DeepSeek V4.1 capture accuracy on PR commit `a59d604c945ed149bfbf597468ff05fbea73ec3a`.

**Environment:** 8× H20 (GPU 0–7), `vllm_liam`. The three TP8 rows use the complete DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash weights and generic MoERunner/MXFP4 Marlin. The DP4/TP2 row uses a **reduced V4.1 configuration with dummy weights** (4 routed layers, 8 experts) because the complete 475 GiB checkpoint cannot fit at TP2 on 96 GiB H20s. That row exercises the V4.1 routing/capture and DP/EP/SP integration, not full-model weight loading.

**Capture accuracy:** An independent oracle recomputed each layer's router top-k IDs before expert dispatch without calling the capturer or restorer. I compared valid device-buffer entries element by element with that oracle and checked returned `routed_experts` at each client token position. Each row ran two rounds.

| Model / mode | Parallelism and execution | Input / output tokens; concurrency | Requests | Buffer mismatches | Shared-restorer calls |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| V4.1 full weights, long-input stress | DP1/TP8, FULL Graph, no EP/SP | 512 or 1024 / 128; C16 | 32 | 0 / 54,988,800 | 4,800 |
| V4.1 full weights, high-concurrency stress | DP1/TP8, FULL Graph (capture size 32), no EP/SP | 128 or 256 / 64; C32 | 64 | 0 / 31,334,400 | 2,880 |
| V4.1 **reduced config, dummy weights** | DP4/TP2, EP/SP, FULL Graph | 128 or 256 / 64; C8 per DP rank | 64 total | 0 / 1,395,936 | 864 |
| V4.1 full weights | DP1/TP8, EP (no SP), PIECEWISE Graph | 128 or 256 / 64; C8 | 16 | 0 / 13,933,440 | 8,960 |

Returned route IDs also had **0 mismatches** in every row. The two full-weight stress rows checked 6,873,600 and 3,916,800 returned IDs, respectively; the DP4/TP2 dummy row checked 391,680; the full-weight PIECEWISE row checked 979,200. Execution counters confirmed graph-path use: 254 and 127 FULL graph replays per GPU for the stress rows, 154 FULL replays per GPU for DP4/TP2, and 127 PIECEWISE graph calls per GPU for the final row.

V4.1 Engram rejects DBO/microbatching at configuration validation, so **DBO was not enabled** in these V4.1 cases. The test-side shared restorer delegates the existing recovery algorithm; these tests validate binding and capture integration, not a separate backend restoration algorithm. No performance claim is made here.

The current PR head is `2a6aefb1456cc743e3f6d7a992dae2e3cbc31962`; relative to the tested commit, only test files changed, not the production capture implementation. The exact current head was not GPU-rerun.
